column2: Search cannot reliably reach a mechanism absent from its representational language; add or discover a testable mechanism before spending more aim budget.
Once a mechanism is reachable, targeting can improve efficiency; it is not proof of new representational power.
column4: compare targeting to equal-budget broad search

column2: A failed hypothesis or tool should create an explicit alternative branch and a discriminating repair test, not a rewritten success story.
column4: preserve failure receipt and precommit the repair test

column2: A learned policy has no advantage claim unless every baseline receives the same inputs, actions, restarts, and resource budget.
Isolation claims require active target-channel, shared-state, and post-hoc-result attacks; a sandbox alone does not remove an encoded target.
column4: run hostile leak audit before accepting a positive

column2: A repaired or forged tool is earned only when it helps a distinct held-out artifact under the same stated boundary.
Prior claims are evidence, not truth: classify scope and provenance, then reproduce a matched claim with a separate worker.
column4: treat mismatched or unverified claims as hypotheses

column2: Strong fixed and broad policies are serious competitors; a tie or loss is a negative result, not evidence of learning.
column4: retain fixed broad random replay and ablation controls

column2: A claim invalidated by a later audit must be removed from actionable method memory while retaining its failure mode as an audit warning.
column4: invalidate dependent positive rules and keep only the warning

column2: Later audits can invalidate attractive positives
column4: block invalidated strategy and rerun audit
